question.text: Where technical limitations prevent required originator or beneficiary information accompanying a cross-border wire transfer from remaining with a related domestic wire transfer, what must the receiving intermediary institution do?

answer.text: Preserve a record of the information for at least six years
File an STR with FIU-IND within 24 hours
Request the originating bank to resend the transfer with complete information

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM IFSCA-01 workbook (p82), where technical limitations prevent the required originator or beneficiary information accompanying a cross-border wire transfer from remaining with a related domestic wire transfer, the receiving intermediary institution must preserve a record of that information for at least six years. The Trap: The technical-limitation scenario does not trigger automatic rejection of the wire transfer or an STR within 24 hours; the workbook position is record preservation for at least six years. Note: The six-year preservation rule is specifically tied to the cross-border-to-related-domestic context — it should not be generalised to every domestic wire transfer where originator information is missing.
